decisions.reason: The rejection reverses the role of a counterexample carrier: its Statement refuted is the false universal implication, while its Jordan-block witness disproves that implication. The definition correctly restricts the order to self-adjoint operators and cites the counterexample only to show why spectral nonnegativity is insufficient without self-adjointness.

The theorem is correct and already cited the spectrum theorem that supplies nonemptiness, but A4 and step 1.2 stated only compactness while the represented compact set is required to be nonempty. The repair now carries both properties explicitly from the cited Banach-algebra spectrum theorem.

A3 was ill-typed for the zero vector, since Tx=lambda x would then impose no spectral condition and f(lambda) might be undefined. The actual basis-vector application uses nonzero e_n. The repaired fact states nonzero eigenvector, derives lambda in the spectrum, and types f(lambda) correctly.

A1 and A2 license real spectral containment and polynomial spectral mapping, not the extra nonempty-compact assertion in step 1.2. That assertion is unnecessary: A5 applied to the already proved normal operator p(T) supplies the attained spectral-radius maximum used in step 2.1. The repair removes only the unsupported surplus claim.

The displayed theorem quantified over self-adjoint operators without boundedness, making its operator norm and spectral minimum and maximum unavailable for standard unbounded examples. Every dependency and proof step works in B(H). The repaired statement now explicitly assumes T in B(H), matching the proof and page scope.

The norm computation replaced |T|*|T| by |T|^2 without first licensing self-adjointness of the positive root. The repair proves that implication locally by polarization of |T|-|T|*, then writes the adjoint-product identity explicitly before using |T|^2=T*T.

The character-space homeomorphism alone does not state that its source is nonempty compact Hausdorff. That topology is required both to make the spectrum nonempty compact and to invoke Stone-Weierstrass. The repair declares the maximal-ideal-space theorem directly and carries its hypotheses through A1 and step 1.1.

A1 literally equated f(T) and g(T) for arbitrary functions when T is self-adjoint, contradicted by the constant zero and one functions. The intended supplier interface is equality of the normal and self-adjoint calculi on the same input function. The repair states that function-by-function agreement precisely.

A7 attributed two facts to a definition that supplied neither, and its character-separation claim is false for arbitrary commutative Banach algebras. Neither assertion is needed. The repair derives f(T)=cI from unital linearity and computes sigma(cI)={c} directly from the bounded-inverse definition.

The Jordan-block computation already refutes the stated universal implication, but the final sentence additionally claimed the self-adjoint spectral-order equivalence without a supplier. That extra claim is unnecessary. The repair closes only from the explicit witness: spectrum {0}, non-real quadratic value, and failure of self-adjointness.

For x=0 the cyclic subspace is the zero space, outside the nonzero-Hilbert-space interface of the supplied calculus, so the unqualified restriction claim was undefined. The repair separates x=0 and proves cyclicity for x nonzero by restricting star-polynomial approximants into C*(I,T|H_x).

A3 asserted the indicator multiplier's range, kernel, and closedness from definitions that did not prove those facts. The repair reduces A3 to the L2 support convention and proves the identities directly using Pg=g on supported classes, Ph=0 on the complement, P^2=P, and bounded limit preservation.

Logical validity does not require a theorem to be independent of its construction. Clauses 1-4 are correctly deduced from the cited PVM-integral and calculus interfaces, while steps 1.2-2.1 give a complete scalar-measure uniqueness argument for the commutant clause. Redundancy with a definition is not a defect.

The cited carrier is a counterexample: its Statement refuted is the false assertion that every bounded normal operator has an eigenvector, while its proof exhibits M_x on L2([0,1]) with spectrum [0,1] and no nonzero eigenvectors. The remark accurately describes that witness and its multiplicity significance.

The proof correctly excludes E([0,1/2]) from the continuous calculus, but its last sentence generalized from that witness to every discontinuous indicator. Null spectral sets can yield the zero projection, a continuous-calculus value. The repair limits the conclusion to the computed half-interval projection.

The opening real-spectrum inference was true but not part of the cited self-adjoint calculus statement, so the scalar real-valued functions were not licensed from the declared interface. The repair adds and cites the dedicated real-spectrum lemma in the dependency list, example setup, and A1.

The definition permits multiplicity zero on null sets, whereas the intertwiner lemma requires values in {1,2,...,infinity} everywhere. The repair changes each multiplicity to one only on its zero null set, proves the L2 model and coordinate multiplier are unchanged, and applies the lemma to those typed representatives.

The cyclic-vector definition did not by itself prove that ambient and restricted calculi generate the same subspace. The repair proves both inclusions: ambient star-polynomial limits preserve the reducing summand, while restricted calculus vectors are limits of restricted star-polynomials equal to ambient polynomial actions.

The contour proof established equality of the two projections but did not justify calling the isolated spectral point an eigenvalue. The repair observes that its singleton indicator is a nonzero continuous function, so the isometric calculus makes E({lambda}) nonzero; the spectral-projection corollary then gives a nonzero eigenspace.

reviews.reason: The quadratic-form relation is correctly defined only on bounded self-adjoint operators, and the polarization argument proves antisymmetry. The companion reference accurately points to a non-self-adjoint Jordan block with spectrum {0} and a non-real quadratic-form value.

A4 now states that the operator spectrum is nonempty and compact and identifies the exact nonzero unital Banach-algebra supplier. Step 1.2 therefore constructs the required nonempty compact K as sigma(T), while the two normality implications remain unchanged.

The local calculus fact now requires a nonzero eigenvector and explicitly records lambda in sigma(T). Step 3.1 applies it to the unit basis vector e_n after step 2.1 has independently computed the full spectrum, so every scalar evaluation is well defined.

Step 1.2 now states exactly the two conclusions supplied by A1 and A2. Step 2.1 obtains the maximum from A5 for the normal operator p(T) and transports its spectrum through polynomial spectral mapping, so the isometric formula and well-defined restriction-class calculus follow without a citation gap.

The theorem now assumes a bounded self-adjoint T in B(H), so the nonempty compact real spectrum, its extrema, the continuous calculus, and the operator norm are all defined. The proof then establishes the order bounds, sharpness, and endpoint norm identity exactly as stated.

The definition now derives self-adjointness of the positive square root directly from real quadratic-form values and polarization. Consequently the displayed chain uses |T|*|T|=|T|^2 legitimately, proving equal pointwise norms, equal kernels, and equal operator norms.

A1 now cites the theorem asserting that the character space of the nonzero unital commutative C*-algebra is nonempty compact Hausdorff. The homeomorphism then transfers nonempty compactness to sigma(T), and Stone-Weierstrass applies on the licensed compact Hausdorff domain in the uniqueness proof.

A1 now says that for self-adjoint T the two constructions assign the same operator to each common function, rather than equating arbitrary f(T) and g(T). All proof uses require only the homomorphism, isometry, and same-input agreement properties, so the stated calculus laws remain fully established.

The constant-function boundary case is now proved from the calculus and resolvent interfaces: unital linearity gives cI, and (lambda-c)I has a bounded inverse precisely off c. The main proof still obtains spectral mapping from character values plus C*-spectral permanence and proves normality algebraically.

The counterexample now concludes strictly from its computed Jordan block. Since J has spectrum {0} but its quadratic form takes i/2 at a unit vector, it satisfies the rejected antecedent and violates positivity; no uncited converse theorem about self-adjoint operators remains in the proof.

The zero-vector branch now stops at H_0={0} and explicitly avoids applying the nonzero-space calculus. For x nonzero, reducing invariance identifies restrictions of star-polynomial approximants with polynomials in the restricted operator, placing the original dense orbit inside the restricted calculus orbit and proving cyclicity.

Step 2.1 now proves both support identities in the quotient L2 space and proves closedness by passing convergent sequences through the bounded idempotent P. Thus the claimed projection has exactly the stated range and kernel without treating a bare definition as a theorem.

The five conclusions follow from the spectral PVM construction and the bounded PVM integral. In particular equality of regular scalar measures is established from continuous test functions, then extended to bounded Borel integrals to prove S h(T)=h(T) S for every bounded Borel h.

The remark correctly distinguishes direct-integral fiber multiplicity from eigenspace dimension and cites the multiplication operator M_x, whose singleton spectral projections vanish and whose eigenvalue equation forces every candidate vector to vanish almost everywhere. Its orientation boundary is also explicit.

The final step now states only what steps 2.1-3.1 prove: equality with E([0,1/2]) would force f=1 on the left interval and f=0 on the right, contradicting continuity at 1/2. It no longer makes a false assertion about arbitrary Borel sets or null spectral projections.

The example now obtains sigma(T) subset R from the exact real-spectrum lemma before defining absolute value, positive and negative parts, and sign on that domain. The Borel homomorphism then transports all scalar identities, and positive-square-root uniqueness identifies the two absolute-value constructions.

The direct implication now normalizes multiplicities on null sets before invoking the intertwiner lemma. Null-set changes leave every level-set L2 summand and M_z unchanged, and the lemma yields equality for the normalized representatives, which immediately descends to equality of the original multiplicities almost everywhere.

Step 1.1 now rigorously proves H_{x_j}=H_j. Reducing invariance gives the ambient-orbit inclusion, and the onto restricted calculus plus star-polynomial approximation gives the reverse inclusion from cyclicity of x_j for T|H_j. The direct-sum unitaries and intertwining then follow as stated.

After proving the contour equals E({lambda}), the verification now uses clopenness of the isolated singleton and the isometric continuous calculus to obtain norm one for that projection. Its range is the eigenspace ker(T-lambda I), so lambda is genuinely an eigenvalue and the title and conclusion are proved.
